## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 6b3ab5d1791ad07bc3af4fe8bb3e57b6ed2a9662

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit swaps the order of two statements in `FileHistoryPanelImpl`'s constructor: `myPopupActions = createPopupActions();` is moved to run *before* `createDualView();` instead of after. This is described as an "initialisation order issue" causing an `IllegalArgumentException` in `PopupHandler.installPopupHandler`. I walked the full `git log -p` history of `FileHistoryPanelImpl.java`, tracking every place `createDualView()` and `myPopupActions = createPopupActions()` appeared, to find when this ordering became unsafe.

**(2) The bug-introducing change:** Even long before the bug, `createDualView()` was called before `myPopupActions` was assigned — but that was safe because `createDualView()` registered popups via *anonymous* `PopupHandler` subclasses that only read the `myPopupActions` field lazily, inside `invokePopup()`, i.e., only when a user actually right-clicked (well after the constructor had finished). Commit `6b3ab5d1791ad07bc3af4fe8bb3e57b6ed2a9662` ("vcs: use util method") refactored this to call the utility method directly:
```java
PopupHandler.installPopupHandler(myDualView.getTreeView(), myPopupActions, ActionPlaces.UPDATE_POPUP, ActionManager.getInstance());
```
`PopupHandler.installPopupHandler`'s `group` parameter is annotated `@NotNull` and is evaluated eagerly at call time — but at the time this line executes inside `createDualView()`, `myPopupActions` is still `null` (it's assigned a few lines later in the constructor). This directly causes the `IllegalArgumentException` reported in EA-79438.

**(3) Supporting evidence:**
- `git show 6b3ab5d1791ad07bc3af4fe8bb3e57b6ed2a9662^:.../FileHistoryPanelImpl.java` confirms the pre-existing (harmless) order: `createDualView()` at line 401, `myPopupActions = createPopupActions()` at line 406.
- The diff of `6b3ab5d17...` shows the replacement of the lazy anonymous-class popup registration with the eager `PopupHandler.installPopupHandler(..., myPopupActions, ...)` calls — the exact API named in the bug title.
- `PopupHandler.java` declares `installPopupHandler(..., @NotNull final ActionGroup group, ...)`, so passing a null `myPopupActions` throws `IllegalArgumentException`.
- `git log --oneline` shows no other commits touched this file between `6b3ab5d17...` and the fix `6caccbbaeae`, so no intervening change could have caused or masked the bug — the causal chain is direct and isolated.

I'm confident in this identification; the mechanism (eager vs. lazy field read) cleanly explains why the pre-existing statement order was safe before this commit and unsafe after it.
